en.title: He Xi 2077 AI Deep Signal Weekly 2026 W45: Execution Foundation, Acceptance Debt, and the Boundaries of Memory
en.summary:
This week's AI news briefing: covering November 2–8, 2026 — agent competition is shifting from models to execution systems, verification infrastructure needs continuous maintenance, and the utility and permission risks of long-term memory have to be accounted for separately.

This week's AI news revolves around "execution foundations, acceptance debt, and memory boundaries," rounding up key product developments, industry trends, and risk signals.

Journal. 2026 W45 • 2026/11/08

This week's keywords: execution foundations / acceptance debt / memory boundaries

Editor's note: Once agents start accumulating experience, rewriting workflows, and acting continuously, what becomes genuinely scarce is no longer the next chunk of output, but traceable state, trustworthy acceptance, and decision rights that remain in human hands.

Coverage period: November 2–8, 2026. This issue draws on seven complete daily reports, 194 news items in total, 193 of which include links to the original source text. Items are deduplicated and selected by topic; repeated daily coverage is not treated as independent corroboration. All experimental figures below belong to the respective authors or publishers and do not represent independent replication by this publication.
en.reason: Covering November 2–8, 2026, the weekly digest distills 194 AI news items into agent execution foundations, acceptance debt, and memory boundaries, citing HEELO’s 46 tasks and Terminal-Bench’s roughly 30% benchmark problems as lingering verification work.

en.title: MaxxBench – "DeepSWE scores well. But is it real?
en.reason: MaxxBench changed 89 DeepSWE tasks with a median reference-patch increase of just 17 lines (3.5%), and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 76.4% versus Gemini 3.8 Flash's 53.4%—a 23-point gap—as models talked themselves out of following changed requirements.

items.title: 再见 Claude，你好 Pi / Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi

sources.title: 再见 Claude，你好 Pi / Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi
sources.summary:
Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi
21 September 2026 #pi #claude
I’ve been a longtime Claude Code user, ever since it became available in the Claude Pro subscription plan over a year ago. I remember the first time I used it, feeling giddy as it spat out messy Python code for whatever random weekend project I was working on, all from a single prompt. I’m certain that in a few years we’ll all look back at its release as one of the major drivers of this new era of software development we’re in.
Despite this,
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 作者因AGENTS.md支持太晚和VSCode仅单会话连接IDE等小挫折弃用Claude Code转投Pi，并指出今年244次发布中超3/4改动系统提示，裁掉80%系统提示后开销仍高于Pi。

en.reason: A longtime Claude Code user switches to Pi after late AGENTS.md support and VSCode's single-session IDE restriction, noting 244 releases this year, over three-quarters touching the system prompt, and that cutting 80% of it still costs more than Pi.
